summary_en: Sanwayuka revised full-year operating profit guidance for fiscal year ending March 2027 upward by 600 million yen (35.3%) to 2,300 million yen and net income by 400 million yen (36.4%) to 1,500 million yen, citing strong performance in recycling and fine chemicals. Final dividend per share raised 10 yen to 60 yen.
title_en: Notice regarding Difference between Interim Consolidated Earnings Forecast for the Second Quarter of Fiscal Year ending March 2027 and Actual Results, Upward Revision of Full-Year Consolidated Earnings Forecast, and Modification (Increase) of Final Dividend Forecast
translation_en_brief:
Sanwayuka reported interim results for the six months ended September 30, 2026 that exceeded previous guidance across major metrics. Operating profit reached 1,272 million yen against a forecast of 800 million yen, a 59.1% increase; net income attributable to parent company shareholders reached 815 million yen against a forecast of 520 million yen, a 56.9% increase. The company attributed this outperformance to strong performance in its recycling and resource circulation business, driven by heightened resource recovery demand following elevated crude oil and naphtha prices amid Middle East tensions, and to recovery in its fine chemicals segment supported by brisk activity in semiconductors and batteries.

Based on interim performance and expectations for sustained high selling prices of regenerated organic solvents and increased waste handling volumes, the company raised its full-year guidance for fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. Operating profit forecast was increased 600 million yen (35.3%) to 2,300 million yen; net income forecast was increased 400 million yen (36.4%) to 1,500 million yen. Sales guidance was raised 2,300 million yen (9.8%) to 25,800 million yen, with full-year results expected to reach record highs.

In line with the earnings upgrade, the company increased its final dividend forecast per share by 10 yen to 60 yen for fiscal year 2027, maintaining its basic policy of stable, non-declining dividends while balancing necessary capital investment and financial soundness.
